With or without food (food eases GI upset)
Use only if clearly needed; generally considered low risk

summary: Cefadroxil is an oral first-generation cephalosporin active mainly against Gram-positive cocci (staphylococci, streptococci) and some Gram-negative uropathogens (E. coli, Proteus, Klebsiella). It is acid-stable, well absorbed and has a relatively long half-life permitting once- or twice-daily dosing. Used for skin, pharyngitis/tonsillitis and uncomplicated urinary tract infections. Requires dose reduction in renal impairment.
indications: Urinary tract infections caused by E. coli, P. mirabilis and Klebsiella species
Skin and skin structure infections caused by staphylococci and/or streptococci
Pharyngitis and/or tonsillitis caused by Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A beta-hemolytic streptococci)

dosage.d: 1 g/day in single or 2 divided doses
1-2 g/day in single (q.d.) or divided doses
dosage.n: Other UTIs: 2 g/day in 2 divided doses

dosage.d: 1 g/day in single or 2 divided doses

dosage.n: Pharyngitis: 30 mg/kg/day once or in 2 doses x 10 days

dosage.d: Initial 1 g, then 500 mg: CrCl 25-50 q12h, 10-25 q24h, 0-10 q36h

admin: Cefadroxil is acid-stable and may be given without regard to meals
Administration with food can diminish GI complaints sometimes seen with oral cephalosporins
Shake suspension well before each dose and measure with an appropriate device
Complete the full prescribed course; for streptococcal pharyngitis treat at least 10 days
moa: Cefadroxil is a bactericidal beta-lactam that binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits the transpeptidation step of bacterial cell-wall peptidoglycan synthesis. The resulting weakened cell wall leads to autolysis and bacterial death. As a first-generation agent it has strong activity against Gram-positive cocci and limited Gram-negative coverage.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to cefadroxil or other cephalosporins
relative: History of penicillin allergy (risk of cross-reactivity)

preg: There are no adequate well-controlled studies in pregnant women; cephalosporins are generally regarded as having a low risk profile. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: Cefadroxil is excreted in human milk in low concentrations and is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding; observe the infant for diarrhea, thrush or rash.
renal: Dosage reduction is required in renal impairment. After an initial 1 g loading dose, give 500 mg at intervals based on creatinine clearance: every 12 hours for CrCl 25-50 mL/min, every 24 hours for 10-25 mL/min, and every 36 hours for 0-10 mL/min.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is required for hepatic impairment; cefadroxil is eliminated largely unchanged by the kidneys.

major: No major contraindicated interactions established for cefadroxil
moderate: Probenecid - reduces renal tubular secretion, raising and prolonging cefadroxil levels
Anticoagulants - cephalosporins may rarely potentiate effect
minor: Live typhoid and BCG vaccines - antibacterials may reduce efficacy
interactions.food: May be taken with food to reduce gastrointestinal upset; food does not impair absorption appreciably.
interactions.alcohol: No clinically significant interaction; cefadroxil does not cause a disulfiram-like reaction.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause a false-positive urine glucose test with copper-reduction methods (Benedict's/Fehling's) and a positive direct Coombs test.

monitoring: Clinical response and resolution of infection
Renal function in patients with impairment or on nephrotoxic drugs
Signs of hypersensitivity, especially in penicillin-allergic patients
Persistent or severe diarrhea (evaluate for C. difficile)
counsel: Complete the entire prescribed course, even if you feel better
May be taken with or without food; with food if it upsets your stomach
Report rash, hives, difficulty breathing or severe/persistent diarrhea promptly
Tell your provider about any prior penicillin or cephalosporin allergy
pk: Antibacterial effect within hours of absorption
Sustained urinary levels allow once/twice-daily dosing
Store at controlled room temperature; reconstituted suspension refrigerate and discard after 14 days
pearls: Longer half-life than cephalexin allows once- or twice-daily dosing
Good choice for Group A streptococcal pharyngitis and uncomplicated skin infection
Cross-reactivity with penicillins is low but possible - take an allergy history
Dose must be extended in renal impairment to avoid accumulation
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule; do not double up.
overdose: Overdose may cause nausea, vomiting, epigastric distress and diarrhea. There is no specific antidote; manage with supportive care. Hemodialysis can remove cefadroxil and may be considered in severe overdose with renal failure.
